subject: Intro & Discovery Recap — Dedicated Capacity Sizing for AcmeCloud
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acmecloud.io>, AcmeCloud Infrastructure Team <infra@acmecloud.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Intro & Discovery Recap — Dedicated Capacity Sizing for AcmeCloud

Hi Jenna / Acme infra team,

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciate the thorough rundown of your current inference flow and the traffic profile. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we can align on a sizing plan: 

Key points we captured
- Workload: primarily real-time customer-facing NLU tasks (intent classification + slot filling) with occasional long-form summarization.
- Current average: ~3M tokens/day; expected growth to ~7–8M tokens/day in peak months.
- Latency target (p95): <= 120ms for single-turn requests; some multi-turn flows can tolerate up to 400ms.
- Peak concurrency: 120 qps sustained for 10–15 minute bursts, occasional spikes to ~220 qps.
- Data controls: VPC + KMS, customer-managed keys preferred.

Next step: schedule a 45–60 minute Dedicated Capacity Sizing call (technical deep-dive) where our infra SE (Monica) will run through: expected RPS profiles, target p95/p99 latencies, batch/caching strategy, and a preliminary capacity estimate with GPU/slot recommendations.

Proposed time slots (PST):
- Thu Aug 5, 10:00–11:00 AM PT
- Thu Aug 5, 2:00–3:00 PM PT
- Fri Aug 6, 9:00–10:00 AM PT

Attachments: discovery notes and a short capacity template to capture exact request/sequence length distributions — please fill if you can before the call.
[Attachment: acme-discovery-notes.pdf]
[Attachment: redwood-capacity-template.xlsx]

If those times don't work, send a couple of alternatives and we'll align. If procurement/legal needs to join that initial sizing call for any commitment/contract questions, feel free to cc them.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Dylan, thanks for the clear recap and for pulling the template together. Helpful.

Thursday (Aug 5) looks promising for us — likely better in the afternoon PT window. If possible, can we do Thu Aug 5 at 2:00 PM PT? That would be 5:00 PM ET for our east coast folks but still workable.

Attendees on our side: myself (infra lead), Miguel Torres (platform engineer), and I've looped in procurement (procurement@acmecloud.io) to stay in the chain. We'll also send a short architecture sketch prior to the call — attaching a very rough diagram.

Agenda request: could you include a 10–15 minute section on fallback and graceful degradation? We had a recent incident where fallback behavior mattered more than raw throughput, so we'd like to validate SLO behavior under partial outages.

Thanks — confirm the time and we'll calendar it.

Best,
Jenna

Hi all — looking forward to the call today at 2:00 PM PT. Quick pre-read from my side so we can use the time efficiently:

1) Proposed 60-minute agenda- 0–10: Introductions & goals- 10–25: Workload profile & sequence length walk-through (we'll reference the template)- 25–45: Sizing + GPU recommendations (including quantization options)- 45–55: Graceful degradation & fallback strategies- 55–60: Action items & next steps

2) Key data I will reference (please send if available):- Typical request/response token distribution- Observed p99 latency and if you have p999 samples- Any multi-turn flows that require KV cache reuse across minutes

3) Quick note on test plan: we'll propose a short throughput validation test (10–20 minute ramp) to validate p95/p99 targets before a full rollout.

I've attached a short internal checklist we use to speed the sizing call and capture config choices. If you can pre-fill even a few rows that will speed us up.
[Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing-checklist.docx]

See you at 2pm PT.

Best,
